clue.text: Starmer notes unruly protests

indicators.note: unruly letters will not stay in line, so STARMER NOTES get rearranged

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's memos are causing unrest in the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the UK Prime Minister; his name plus NOTES supplies exactly the twelve letters. 'Protests' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to protest or object forcefully.

clue.text: Pilloried, as one's Sunday lunch may be

definitions.meaning: to roast someone is to mock them mercilessly

definitions.text: as one's Sunday lunch may be
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the adjective ROASTED
definitions.meaning: the Sunday roast, meat cooked in the oven

explanation.walkthrough: A Sunday roast is the traditional British Sunday lunch of roasted meat and vegetables. The first sense is the comic 'roast': to mock someone mercilessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone roasted has been savagely criticised, and a Sunday joint is literally roasted.

clue.text: Satirical host entertaining old ruler

indicators.note: a host entertains guests inside the house, so the host's letters go round 'old'

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued chat-show host has a retired monarch as a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old ruler' reads as one unit, a former king, but it splits: 'old' goes inside the host, and 'ruler' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and satirical both describe ridicule aimed at a target.

clue.text: Avoided disaster on earth ingeniously, to an extent

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining a noun: a near thing is a disaster narrowly avoided

indicators.note: only part of the phrase 'on earth ingeniously' is used, so the answer sits inside it

parts.note: the letters run across all three words, from the end of 'on' to four letters into 'ingeniously'

explanation.surface: Humanity cleverly dodged catastrophe, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a near thing is the close call itself, so 'Avoided disaster' has to be read as 'a disaster only just avoided'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: when something was a near thing it only just missed going wrong, so disaster was avoided by a whisker.

clue.text: American takeaway in African country

definitions.note: defines the two-word American phrase TO GO
definitions.meaning: the two-word US phrase for food bought to eat elsewhere
a small West African state between Ghana and Benin

explanation.surface: Someone orders a US-style takeaway meal while in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US, food 'to go' is what the British call a takeaway. Run together, TO GO is the West African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a country in West Africa, and 'to go' is American for takeaway.

clue.text: A couple of Liberals on the Tories' side? I'll allow it

definitions.note: a whole phrase standing for the interjection ALL RIGHT

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'on' puts one piece below the other

parts.note: the Conservatives, or Tories, sit on the political right

explanation.surface: A speaker lets two Liberal MPs cross the floor to join the Conservative side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are the UK Conservative Party, the party of the right. The question mark flags the surface's parliamentary joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'All right' grants permission, just as 'I'll allow it' does.

clue.text: Summon sinner to receive fine

indicators.note: the sinner takes in the next word, so it goes inside her

parts.note: Eve ate the forbidden fruit, the first sinner in Genesis

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is called to court to be handed a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty in a court scene, but it means OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up or summon a memory or feeling.

clue.text: Louise's partner playing Hamlet

indicators.note: letters at play move about

explanation.surface: An actress's partner has been cast as the Prince of Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing Hamlet' looks like a stage role; 'playing' is the shuffle instruction instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma and Louise are the two fugitive heroines of the 1991 film.

clue.text: Dealt with leaders of the Republicans and Democrats, ending dispute

indicators.note: the leading letter of each word that follows is taken

parts.words: the Republicans and Democrats, ending dispute
parts.note: first letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A negotiator brokers peace between the two US parties' heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of' looks like it governs only the two parties, but it runs all the way to 'dispute', taking the initial of every word, 'ending' included.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to deal, as a dealer in goods does.

clue.text: Divine messenger has American coins in both hands

indicators.note: the coins sit inside the two hands

parts.note: R and L, right and left hand; it will hold the coins

explanation.surface: An angel appears clutching a fistful of US cents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American coins' begs to be CENTS or DIMES; 'American' is just A, and the coins are CHANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is a chief angel, and 'angel' itself means messenger.

clue.text: Alternative admitted by psychotherapist

indicators.note: the word lets the answer in, so it is held inside

parts.note: five letters starting at the fifth letter of the word

explanation.surface: A therapist confesses to using an alternative treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitted' looks like confessed, but it means let in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: choosing the other road means choosing the alternative.

clue.text: Dickensian boy gets capital from Scrooge — such events are surprising

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase; twists are surprising events

parts.note: Oliver Twist, the orphan in Dickens's novel

indicators.note: a capital is a first letter

explanation.surface: An orphan gets money from the miser, which would be a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money from a miser, but here it means an initial letter. It is apt: Oliver Twist famously asked for more.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist in a plot is a sudden unexpected turn, so the plural names events that surprise.

clue.text: Defamed beautiful woman in cap

indicators.note: the woman is put inside the cap

explanation.surface: A pretty woman in a hat has been slandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' reads as headwear worn by the woman, but it is a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: To libel someone is to defame them in writing.

clue.text: Follow guide at intervals, getting child's pet

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, skipping the gaps

explanation.surface: Trailing a guide now and then earns someone a young one's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow' opens the clue like a verb of instruction, but it gives DOG, a neat echo of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggie is the childish word for a dog.

clue.text: Handouts reallocated, which is grand

indicators.note: letters reallocated are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Benefit payments have been redistributed, which is excellent news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like an adjective of approval, but it is the noun: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars, so the noun stands for the number.

clue.text: Sultan due to travel around in Rolls

indicators.note: letters that travel around end up in new places

explanation.surface: A sultan is expected to be chauffeured about in a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like the luxury car, the Rolls-Royce, but it is the verb: moves in waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that undulates rolls up and down in waves.

clue.text: Helping a learner using logic

parts.note: a helping is a portion, a ration
L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Someone assists a student by reasoning things through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb, assisting, but it is a noun: a serving of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means based on reason, using logic.

clue.text: Student is glummer, gutted after job advert

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters
the gutted word comes after the job

parts.note: G(lumme)R, only the outer letters kept

explanation.surface: A student grows gloomier and is devastated after seeing a job listing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, which fits the glum student; here it means emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortening: informal for someone studying after a first degree, a kind of student.

clue.text: Remedy that hurts? It offers comfort after retiring

parts.note: OW is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A painful cure followed by relief once one has gone to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reads as giving up work, but it means going to bed; the definition is a cryptic description.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow gives comfort once you have retired to bed.

clue.text: Star man in Barbie is depressed

explanation.surface: The leading man of the Barbie film is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star man in Barbie' reads as the actor who played Ken in the 2023 film; it splits into a star and the doll.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken ground is depressed, lying lower than its surroundings.

clue.text: Fan did act when ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in order, a new one

explanation.surface: A devotee performed on demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' could be the cooling device or the verb; it is an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal extension: someone hooked on a hobby, as in a crossword addict, is a devoted fan.

clue.text: The setter's gone over painting technique

parts.note: the setter is I, so 'the setter's' is I'M

explanation.surface: The compiler has gone back over a painting method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone over' reads as a phrasal verb, revisited, but splits into PAST and O. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying paint on thickly.

clue.text: Kid's foot, excessively small, wrapped in accessory

indicators.note: the small letter is wrapped inside the accessory

parts.note: a tie is a clothing accessory; it holds the next letter
S = small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A child's foot, tiny, tucked into a shoe or sock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid's foot' is the definition, not a shoe of kid leather; 'accessory' is something worn, not a partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery word: tootsies are what adults call a small child's toes or feet.

clue.text: Underwear brand worn by Spice Girl

indicators.note: one piece is put on round the other, like clothing

parts.note: a line is a product range or brand
Geri Halliwell, Ginger Spice of the 1990s pop group

explanation.surface: A pop star is modelling a label's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn by' would normally put the thing worn inside the wearer; here the brand is the outer piece, a loose use of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French: the word covers women's underwear and nightwear.

clue.text: Revolutionary books are an inspiration for poets

indicators.note: something that revolves turns round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Radical writings inspire poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary books' reads as seditious literature, but 'Revolutionary' only turns the letters round. The Old Testament is the usual crossword source for 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Syrian city a group of stars tours very quietly

indicators.note: a tour goes all the way round, so the constellation surrounds the next letters

parts.note: pp = pianissimo, the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: A pop group of celebrities makes a discreet visit to a Syrian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' suggests a band of celebrities on tour; it is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major city in northern Syria.

clue.text: European country's heartless PR work

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letter, is removed

parts.note: the country in south-west Europe, whose middle letter then goes

explanation.surface: A cynical view of a nation's public relations campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as belonging to the country but works as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the slanted presentation of news by public relations staff.

clue.text: Wonderful to follow love letter from Athens

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: love = nil = O in tennis scoring
mega is slang for great, wonderful

explanation.surface: A marvellous love letter is on its way from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love letter' is a false unit; 'love' belongs to the wordplay and 'letter from Athens' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Dreadfully inept sots — they show favouritism

indicators.note: done dreadfully, the letters come out in a mess

explanation.surface: Useless drunks in charge who favour their own people.
explanation.walkthrough: A sot is a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotists favour relatives and friends, typically with jobs.

clue.text: One of The Drifters, drunk, messed up notes

parts.note: 'rolling drunk' is so drunk as to be staggering

indicators.note: messed-up letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A member of the soul group The Drifters is drunk and fluffs his notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Drifters is a real band, which pulls towards a band member's name; in fact a rolling stone is a drifter, from 'a rolling stone gathers no moss', and a nod to another band.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling stone is a person who never settles, a drifter.
